summary: The plan-save human-approval gate is correct and well-tested. plan save sets awaiting-approval and only records approved when a marker matches (plan_sha256, issue, story); plan approve --by writes that marker; the marker is consumed on the approved save so it authorizes exactly one save. Five tests cover no-marker refusal, --by requirement plus digest binding, edited-plan/stale-marker refusal, single-use consumption, and that every pre-existing plan-save gate still runs unchanged. The --issue selector serves the real headless/cron case (no run.json), not speculative flexibility. No over-engineering; constitution-mandated structure untouched.

non_blocking_findings.summary: The approved plan is written before the marker is unlinked; a crash between the two would leave an approved plan with a live marker, allowing one re-approval of the same body — a narrow local-CLI crash window, not a normal-path defect.
